title: What is the Average Salary in Turkey​?
description: Learn about the average salary in Turkey, including trends across industries and factors affecting wages. Up-to-date statistics!

breadcrumb.name: What is the Average Salary in Turkey​?

contentHtml:
Turkey is a country straddling two continents. The country presents a unique labor market. It is influenced by a blend of cultural, economic, and geographic factors. However, the average salary in Turkey has seen fluctuations. This is because of the country’s dynamic economic conditions. These can be inflation, the Turkish Lira strength, and shifting global economic trends.

The blog is written to discuss an in-depth analysis of the average salary in Turkey. We will explore the factors that influence salaries. This gives you detailed insights into the country’s labor market.

What is the Average Salary in Turkey​?

The average monthly salary in Turkey ranges between 2,900 TRY to 3,200 TRY. These stats are recorded as the latest data available. Note that, this figure can vary based on multiple factors such as the:

  • Industry
  • Region
  • Education, and
  • Work experience

Generally, salaries in Turkey are higher in major metropolitan areas. These entail Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir. Due to big industries like finance, technology, and manufacturing are prominent.

Urban areas tend to have higher living costs in comparison to rural parts of the country. This is offset by higher wages. A resident of Istanbul might earn more than someone in a smaller town. The cost of living in Istanbul is also higher.

The wage difference is pronounced between the private and public sectors. Private companies are typically known to offer higher salaries. Especially multinational corporations. They do so to attract skilled professionals. On the other hand, government jobs may compensate for lower wages with job security and additional benefits.

Factors That Influence Salaries in Turkey

Several key factors influence the wages of workers in Turkey. Understanding these factors is crucial. Employers and employees know them well when navigating the Turkish labor market.

Economic Sector:

The economic sector in which a person works determines salary levels. Employees in industries such as:

  • Finance
  • Technology, and
  • Healthcare earns more as compared to those sectors like agriculture or retail.

Turkey has become more digitized and tech-oriented. Due to this, sectors like IT, cybersecurity, and digital marketing are seeing a surge in salaries. They do so to attract skilled professionals.

Geographical Location:

It is noted that wages are higher in urban cities like Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir. This is due to the concentration of multinational companies and higher costs of living. Rural areas and smaller towns offer lower salaries in contrast. This disparity is present, it is worth noting that many rural workers face a lower cost of living. It means that compensates for the lower salary levels.

Education and Skills:

The education level and skills of an employee are major factors. These can determine their salary in Turkey. Highly educated individuals with degrees in specialized fields like:

  • Engineering
  • Medicine, or
  • Law, tend to earn higher wages.

Similarly, individuals with advanced technical skills or expertise in high-demand fields can command higher pay. Because of the scarcity of qualified professionals.

Experience:

Experience is also a prominent factor in determining salary ranges. For instance, entry-level positions pay less compared to mid-level and senior roles. Employees see wage increases with more years in the workforce. Individuals with years of experience in highly technical fields may earn salaries well. Their wages are above the national average.

Company Size and Type:

Larger companies and multinational corporations offer:

  • Higher salaries
  • Benefits, and
  • Bonuses compared to smaller, local businesses.

Larger firms have the financial resources to attract and retain top talent. Smaller companies offer fewer perks and lower compensation packages.

Market Demand:

Salaries are also impacted by supply and demand. If a profession is in high demand but there is a limited supply of qualified workers. In this scenario, wages will rise as employers compete to attract the best candidates.

Wages may remain stagnant or decline if there is an oversupply of workers in a particular sector 

Government Legislation:

Minimum wage laws and regulations directly influence salary levels. The Turkish government periodically adjusts the minimum wage. They do so to reflect inflation and changes in the cost of living. As a result, it turn affects wage levels in the public and private sectors.

Unionization:

The presence of strong labor unions can lead to higher wages in some sectors. They promote better benefits, and improved working conditions. Typically, unionized workers have more leverage in negotiating better salaries. They can ask for better working conditions compared to those in non-unionized industries.

What are the Minimal Wages in Turkey (Monthly and Hourly)

The Turkey government sets a minimum wage. It is updated periodically. The purpose is to reflect changes in the economy in inflation rates. The gross monthly minimum wage was 8,506.80 TRY as of early 2023. In comparison to previous years, this is a significant increase. The aim behind this is to mitigate the effects of inflation. By doing so, improving the living standards of lower-income workers.

The net monthly wage that workers take home is lower after deductions for:

  • Income tax
  • Social Security, and
  • Other mandatory contributions

Breaking down the hourly minimum wage for a clearer picture of minimum wage.

Here is the information you provided in a table format:

Description Value
Typical Full-Time Workweek (Turkey) 45 hours/week
Working Hours in a Month 195 hours/month
Gross Hourly Minimum Wage 43.62 TRY/hour

 

In Turkey, the full-time workweek is around 45 hours. There are roughly 195 working hours in a month. It is based on 4.33 weeks per month. The gross hourly minimum wage is approximately 43.62 TRY. This figure offers a baseline for understanding labor costs and wage expectations for entry-level workers.

Exploring the Gender Wage Gap in Turkey

The gender wage gap remains an important issue. Turkey women earn less than men in most sectors. Occupational segregation is the main factor. This contributes to the gender wage gap. Due to this, women are employed in low-paying or part-time roles. Also, societal norms limit women’s access to high-paying positions. They are restrained from obtaining senior management positions.

On average women earn 15-20% less than men. These stats are taken from reports from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat), a comparison of median salaries across sectors. Progress has been seen in female participation in higher education and the workforce. Still, women face substantial barriers to getting wage equality in the workplace.

Several efforts have been made. These are taken to bridge the gender wage gap. Legislative measures were also introduced. It aimed at promoting equal pay for equal work. Moreover, educational initiatives have been introduced. These aimed to support women in traditionally male-dominated fields. Also, government programs encourage entrepreneurship among women.

As we discussed, what is the average salary in Turkey​. Now, we are heading towards to discuss the highest paying occupations in Turkey.

What are the Highest Paying Occupations in Turkey

Certain occupations in Turkey command higher salaries than others. Typically requiring:

  • Specialized education
  • Advanced skills, or
  • High levels of responsibility

Some of the highest-paying jobs in Turkey include:

Senior Executives:

Senior executives involve CEOs, CFOs, and other top executives in large corporations or multinational companies. They are among the highest earners. Due to the complexity and responsibility of their roles.

IT Professionals:

Jobs in software development, data science, and cybersecurity offer lucrative salaries. Given the rise of digitalization, along with IT consulting that provides good packages.

Medical Professionals:

Skilled doctors like surgeons, cardiologists, and specialists in high-demand fields. They can earn significant salaries.

Finance Professionals:

Roles in investment banking, financial analysis, and consulting. They are provided with high compensation packages.

Engineering Experts:

Engineers in fields like petroleum, mining, and civil engineering. All are command high wages due to the technical expertise required.

Legal Professionals:

Lawyers specializing in corporate law or with international experience. These specialist earn high fees for their legal services.

Aviation Professionals:

Pilots and air traffic controllers receive competitive salaries. This is due to the extensive training and responsibility required in the aviation industry.

These roles, though high-paying, involve demanding work environments. They may require significant education and years of experience.

Annual Average Wage Growth in Turkey

Turkey’s wage growth has fluctuated due to economic challenges such as:

  • Inflation
  • Currency depreciation, and
  • Shifting labor market dynamics

Wages tend to rise as businesses thrive in periods of economic growth. The country is in a better position to offer higher compensation. Wage growth may stagnate or decline as companies cut costs. This has been reported during times of economic downturn.

The Turkish government has periodically adjusted the minimum wage in recent years. They do so to reflect inflation. It leads to an increase in the average wage growth. Real wage growth still adjusted for inflation can be slower. This means workers may face a reduction in their purchasing power. In a scenario, if nominal wages increase.

Discovering Compensation Costs in Turkey (Per Hour Worked)

Employers in Turkey must account for compensation costs in addition to direct salaries. This includes:

  • Social security contributions
  • Retirement benefits, and
  • Other labor-related expenses such as taxes and insurance

These indirect costs contribute to the total expense of hiring and maintaining an employee. Employers must contribute to health insurance, unemployment insurance, and pension funds. These can significantly increase the total compensation costs per employee. This is particularly true in larger companies with a high number of employees.

As explored earlier what is the average salary in Turkey​. Let’s explore the wage comparison of Turkey with other countries.

Wage Comparison with Other Countries

In comparison to other countries, Turkey’s average salary falls somewhere in the middle. Turkey’s salary levels are lower than those on a global scale. As compared to the United States, Germany, or the United Kingdom. However, relatively higher than those in Russia, India, or China. This reflects Turkey’s transition from a developing to a developed economy.

Country Average Monthly Salary (USD PPP)
Turkey $900 – $1,000
United States $3,500 – $4,000
Germany $3,000 – $3,500
United Kingdom $2,700 – $3,200
China $1,200 – $1,400
Russia $700 – $800
India $400 – $500

The purchasing power parity is crucial for comparing wages globally. PPP adjusts for local living costs. It reflects the true economic value of wages in different countries.

Conclusion

In conclusion, the salary landscape in Turkey is multifaceted. It is influenced by economic conditions and sectoral demands. The geographical location and government policies also make huge impacts. However, the average salary in Turkey provides a baseline. The true picture can vary widely. It is primarily based on industry, location, and qualifications. Certain high-paying sectors offer competitive wages. Still, the gender wage gap and income inequality remain ongoing challenges.

Turkey continues its economic development and wage growth to bridge the wage gap. The compensation packages they launched, and efforts they are making will be central to improving living standards. As a result, it boosts economic opportunities for its workforce.

FAQs:

What is the current average salary in Turkey?

As of 2026, the average salary in Turkey is around TRY 25,000 to TRY 30,000 per month, depending on the city, industry, and employee experience level.

How is the average salary in Turkey calculated?

The average salary is calculated based on total earnings across all sectors, divided by the number of employed individuals. It includes both private and public sector wages before tax deductions.

Does the average salary differ between cities in Turkey?

Yes, salaries vary by location. Major cities like Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir offer higher wages due to greater living costs and job opportunities, while smaller cities generally have lower salary ranges.

What are the highest-paying sectors in Turkey?

The highest-paying sectors include information technology, engineering, finance, healthcare, and aviation. Skilled professionals in management or technical roles typically earn above the national average.

What is the minimum wage in Turkey, and how does it compare to the average salary?

The minimum wage in Turkey for 2026 is approximately TRY 17,002 per month, which is significantly lower than the national average salary. This gap highlights income differences between entry-level and skilled positions.
